evidence_precedence.meaning: A real requested document was observed printing successfully after the canonical mapping workflow.
For an already logged-on target user, the requested shared queue was connected inside that existing interactive user token and the user's printer-connection registry state was observed.

The requested shared queue is registered under the canonical HKLM per-computer printer connection path by SYSTEM /ga. This is durable registration for all users but is not, by itself, proof that a user who was already logged on has materialized the connection in the current session.
Local queue status, WorkOffline, PortName, CIM, SMB, RPC, or remote Get-Printer observations are diagnostic context only.

forbidden_inferences: SYSTEM /ga plus HKLM registration means an already logged-on user necessarily has the printer in the current session.
A local IP_* or TCP_* PortName proves the canonical mapping failed.
A remote Get-Printer or RPC timeout proves a mapping failure after a real document printed successfully.
Successful real-world printing should be ignored until another synthetic test page is printed.
required_agent_behavior: Keep SYSTEM /ga as the durable all-users registration mechanism.
When a target user is already logged on, materialize the requested queue inside that existing interactive token and verify current-user connection state before reporting the current session ready.
When no target user is logged on, report machine-wide registration as pending next logon rather than claiming immediate user-session availability.
Treat a reported successful real document print after canonical mapping as runtime acceptance evidence for that mapping path.
Do not remap, remove a printer object, delete a port, or request another test page solely to reconcile lower-ranked diagnostic telemetry.
Preserve contradictory telemetry as a warning or diagnostic note unless a later observed failure reopens the incident.
Keep machine-wide registration proof, active-user connection proof, and runtime print acceptance as distinct proof layers rather than conflating them.
